evidence.claim: CNAS argues the defense industrial base remains shallow and fragile, with DoD supply chains averaging five to six tiers and visibility often degrading beyond tier two; this supports the node-level premise that subtier suppliers and traceability can become policy chokepoints.

A media report alleges GE Aerospace has been reviewing suppliers on quality, on-time delivery, OSHA compliance, and domestically sourced raw-material percentages. This is useful as a lead only and requires validation against GE filings, prime-contractor disclosures, and contract databases.
evidence.source_title: GE Aerospace’s Secret Supplier Shakeout Is Rattling Ohio’s Factory Belt – USA Business Times

evidence.claim: Howmet’s 2024 Form 10-K describes products including investment castings for jet engines, aerospace fastening systems, titanium structures, forged jet engine components, machined and forged titanium/aluminum aircraft parts, and Engineered Structures serving aerospace and defense applications.

ATI’s fiscal 2025 Form 10-K states aerospace and defense represented approximately 68% of total sales, and its HPMC segment produces titanium/titanium-based alloys, nickel/cobalt superalloys, precision forgings, components, and machined parts for aerospace and defense markets.

Carpenter Technology disclosures describe the company as producing and distributing premium specialty alloys including titanium alloys, powder metals, stainless steels, alloy steels, and tool steels for critical applications in aerospace, defense, medical, transportation, energy, industrial, and consumer markets.
evidence.source_title: Carpenter Technology 2023 Annual Report on Form 10-K

memory_update.text: HWM should remain the reference anchor for aerospace forgings, castings, fasteners, titanium structures, and machined aerospace components, but it is not the main underfollowed alpha lane.

ATI is a high-priority underfollowed candidate for domestic-material traceability because its aerospace/defense mix is large and its product set includes titanium, nickel/cobalt superalloys, precision forgings, and machined parts.
CRS is a viable specialty-alloy candidate, but later layers must verify current aerospace/defense revenue mix, customer qualification evidence, and domestic-source compliance relevance.

KALU is a low-attention aluminum Aero/HS candidate; later layers should stress-test leverage, cyclicality, packaging exposure, and whether aerospace/high-strength products are large enough to move consolidated results.

Need a follow-up pass for quality/certification/testing providers, ERP/material-traceability software, nondestructive inspection, coatings, and precision-machining specialists that may sit one step away from obvious material suppliers.

summary: Layer 1B expansion for the aerospace/defense domestic-material traceability node. The direct-exposure universe clusters around titanium, nickel/superalloy, aluminum plate/sheet, forgings, castings, fasteners, and precision-machined aerospace components. Reference context is Howmet Aerospace as an obvious scaled leader; underfollowed lane prioritizes ATI, Carpenter Technology, and Kaiser Aluminum because they are closer to specialty-material and semi-fabricated input bottlenecks that could matter if primes and DoD customers tighten domestic-origin documentation, supplier audits, and quality/on-time-delivery compliance. No buy/sell recommendation is implied.
